spans.text: Frankly speaking, most of my exposure to stuff like probabilities came from things you should never attempt.
Uh, so like the probability of death?
No, the probability of a thrill-seeker doing stupid things.
I get it. You mean gambling.
...Are you talking about cheating? In that case, one should be considered a good manipulator of probability!
That's just being a fraud, not a manipulator of probability.
Manipulating probabilities isn't the same as cheating either.
Huh, would you mind explaining it a bit more clearly? I'm interested.
You used to be an accountant? Don't tell me you scam people in that line of work too?
Oh no, that's not the case. We don't manipulate or play with numbers in our line of work. We either fill in the correct numbers, or make up the desired numbers.
Isn't that just cheating with some sugarcoating?
In both cases, you are going to jail.
Of course it's not the same. They'll get sentences with different jail times.
Take gambling as an example.
Say we all flip a coin at the same time. Those who get heads win, others who get tails lose. The winners need to give a coin to the losers.
Suppose now that each of you has two coins and I have a hundred. What would the result be like?
I know, I know! The probability of getting heads and tails is the same, which means the odds of winning and losing are the same.
By the end, we still have two, and you still have a hundred.
Wrong. I will hold onto all 108 coins, and none of you will have a single coin left.
Why?
Because once you lose your two coins, you don't get a third chance to even compete with me.
You see what I mean?
That's nasty...
So what's our point of being here?
Helping AR Team find the true correct probability?
In simpler terms, it's helping them balance out the probability of failure.
What now? I feel even more upset than before!
Hmph. Let's get to the next round then.
I'm not going to admit defeat. Giving up just makes you look the worst!
